data.field_of_study: Linguistics and Bilingualism (Applied Linguistics and Bilingualism pathway; language-related areas including second language acquisition, bilingualism/multilingualism, sociolinguistics, corpus linguistics and related fields)
data.other_hard: English language test: IELTS 6.5 overall with no individual component below 6.5, or Swansea University recognised equivalent (offer may be conditional); must approach a potential supervisor prior to submitting an application; honours degree at first or upper second-class level, or a masters from a UK academic research organisation
data.evidence_sentence: To receive WGSSS studentship funding, you must have qualifications or experience equal to an honours degree at a first or upper second-class level, or a masters from a UK academic research organisation.
data.notes: The name refers to International Research Scholarships, but the page is for a single ESRC WGSSS fully funded PhD (RS997) and states it is open to UK and international applicants. Project start October 2027; the page lists Swansea University (Singleton and Bay campuses). Non-traditional academic backgrounds are welcome to apply (preference, not requirement). Full-time award holders cannot hold a full-time job, and part-time award holders cannot hold a full-time job (conditions during the award, not entry criteria). A 3-month Research in Practice placement is required during the award. Stipend figure given is £21,805 for 2026/27. The page also mentions a possible 1+3 award requiring a separate Master's application, which does not apply to this scholarship as stated. Deferral may be granted in exceptional circumstances (not an entry criterion).
